nodes.description: Public uint256 state variable test1 of contract NFGasNames, unused but part of storage layout.
Public bytes32 state variable test2 of contract NFGasNames, unused but part of storage layout.
Public mapping(uint256 => string) names, the core registry that maps a token id to a name string.
Public IERC721 nfgas reference, set in the constructor to the external NFT contract address.
Constructor(address a) that assigns the external IERC721 contract reference nfgas.
setName(uint256 id, string memory name) public; checks nfgas.ownerOf(id) == msg.sender, verifies keccak256(name) % 1025 == id, then writes names[id] = name.
msg.sender, the caller-controlled address used as the ownership authorization in setName.
Constructor input address a, used as the external NFT contract reference.
setName input uint256 id, the token id / name hash target.
setName input string memory name, the human readable name to register.
Local uint256 hashValue = uint(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(name))) % 1025 used to bind the name to the id.
External call nfgas.ownerOf(id) to an attacker-supplied IERC721 address inside setName, executed before the state write.
State write names[id] = name executed after the external ownerOf call, enabling reentrancy-driven registry overwrite.
Keccak256 hash and modulo 1025 arithmetic used to validate that the name maps to the given id (weak, look-up-able binding).

edges.reason: Constructor parameter a is assigned into the nfgas state variable, tainting the external contract reference with a caller-chosen address.
The constructor body writes the nfgas state variable.
The nfgas state variable is the receiver/target of the external ownerOf call.
The id parameter is passed as the argument to nfgas.ownerOf(id).
msg.sender is compared against the untrusted external ownerOf result to authorize the call.
nfgas is an arbitrary IERC721 supplied at construction time, so ownerOf can execute attacker-controlled code that re-enters setName.
setName executes the external ownerOf call as its first authorization step.
setName performs the keccak256/modulo hash computation and require check.
The name parameter is hashed into the local hashValue variable.
The name parameter feeds the keccak256 hashing inside the modulo arithmetic operation.
hashValue is reduced modulo 1025 as part of the id validation arithmetic.
The id parameter is compared against the modulo result inside the hash validation.
The successful hash/id require check gates the names[id] = name state write.
setName writes the names mapping after all checks pass.
The id parameter is used as the mapping key for the names[id] = name write.
The name parameter is the value stored into the names mapping.
The state write mutates the names mapping state variable.
msg.sender determines which ownership check must pass before the names[id] write is allowed.
msg.sender is the caller identity used for the only access-control check inside setName.

normalization_plan.reason: Constructor parameter a has no independent security identity; it is a plain input that is immediately stored into the nfgas state variable by the constructor.
The id parameter is entirely local to setName, acting only as look-up key and validation operand for the function's logic.
The name parameter is only consumed inside setName (hashed and stored) and carries no standalone vulnerability semantics.
The local hashValue temporary exists solely as the intermediate result of the keccak256 modulo 1025 arithmetic operation and should be folded into it.
